title: Bounds from successful pair decoding
statement: Let $C,c$ be natural numbers and let $w,x',u,x,\mathrm{pad}$ be binary words. Suppose decoding $w$ yields $(x',u)$ and decoding $x'$ yields $(x,\mathrm{pad})$. Then $|x|\le |w|$, and the length of the binary expansion of $C\,(2^{|x|+1})^c$ is at most $(|w|+1)^c$ plus the length of the binary expansion of $C$.
replaced: Let $C, c$ be natural numbers and suppose a string $w$ decodes as a pair with first component $x'$, which in turn decodes as a pair with first component $x$. Then $|x| \le |w|$, and the binary expansion of $C \cdot 2^{(|x|+1)^c}$ has length at most $(|w|+1)^c$ plus the length of the binary expansion of $C$.
